facts.text: The study fabricated HfNbTaTiZr components by 3D ink-extrusion printing followed by de-binding in flowing hydrogen.
The printed components were vacuum-sintered at 1400 °C for 18 h using titanium sponge as an oxygen getter.
Sintering was performed under a vacuum below 3×10^-6 torr.
Phase stabilization was investigated by water-quenching the alloy from 1500 °C.
In-situ alloying proceeded through sequential hydride decomposition associated with formation-enthalpy differences, in the order Ta, Nb, then Hf/Ti/Zr hydrides.
Water quenching suppressed formation of the alpha-HCP phase and retained a metastable beta-BCC phase.
Controlled oxygen uptake of approximately 1.0 wt.% produced interstitial strengthening in the sintered alloy.
The silicide coating resisted oxidation through self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 that filled defects in the protective oxide scale.
Quenching produced a metastable single beta-BCC alloy with a measured grain size of 33 ± 19 µm.
The printed and sintered alloy exhibited excellent high-temperature compressive strength.
The silicide coating reduced the oxidation parabolic rate constant by approximately 700-fold relative to the uncoated baseline.
The coated sample had a parabolic oxidation rate constant of approximately 0.80 mg² cm^-4 h^-1, compared with approximately 570 mg² cm^-4 h^-1 for the uncoated sample.
